facts.fact: The page states that 42% of local searchers click on one of the listings in the Google Map Pack, a figure it does not attribute to a named source.
facts.quote: A massive **42% of local searchers** click on one of the listings in the Google Map Pack.

facts.fact: The page states that customers are 2.7 times more likely to consider a business reputable if it has a complete and detailed local listing, a figure it does not attribute to a named source.
facts.quote: Customers are also **2.7 times more likely** to consider a business reputable if it has a complete and detailed local listing.

facts.fact: The page claims the Google Business Profile is responsible for 32% of Map Pack ranking potential, a figure it does not attribute to a named source.
facts.quote: Your Google Business Profile is now the single biggest ranking factor for the Map Pack, responsible for **32% of your ranking potential**.

facts.fact: The page states that a Google Business Profile business description allows 750 characters.
facts.quote: You get **750 characters** for your business description.

facts.fact: The page defines the Google Map Pack as the block of three businesses with a map shown at the top of local search results.
facts.quote: The Google Map Pack (that block of three businesses with a map you see right at the top of local search results)

facts.fact: The page says copying the same content and only swapping the city name is an old-school spam tactic that Google will penalize.
facts.quote: Don't just copy and paste the same content and swap out the city name. That's an old-school spam tactic that Google will sniff out and penalize.

facts.fact: The page recommends placing your full NAP information in the footer of every single page of the website.
facts.quote: The best practice is to place your full NAP information in the footer of every single page.

facts.fact: The page says the NAP on the website must match the Google Business Profile listing exactly, including punctuation and whether "St." or "Street" is used.
facts.quote: Make sure it perfectly matches your GBP listing, right down to the comma and whether you use "St." or "Street."

facts.fact: The page states that title tags must include the main service and location.
facts.quote: It absolutely must include your main service and location.

facts.fact: The page advises embedding a Google Map on the Contact Us or location page of the website.
facts.quote: Next, go to your "Contact Us" or location page and embed a Google Map showing your business location.

facts.fact: The page advises that businesses should respond to all Google reviews, both good and bad.
facts.quote: You absolutely must respond to _all_ of them, good and bad.

facts.fact: The page says that for citations, quality beats quantity, so being listed correctly on a few authoritative sites is better than on hundreds of junk directories.
facts.quote: When it comes to citations, **quality** beats **quantity** every time.

facts.fact: The page defines a citation as a mention of a business's Name, Address, and Phone number (NAP) on another website, which Google uses to verify business information.
facts.quote: Think of them as digital breadcrumbs scattered across the internet that lead back to you.

facts.fact: The page advises asking for reviews right after a great experience and sending customers a direct link to the Google review form by text or email.
facts.quote: Ask for a review right after you’ve delivered a great experience

facts.fact: The page says a new or newly serious local SEO business should plan on two to six months before seeing consistent Map Pack visibility for its most important search terms (vendor's own estimate).
facts.quote: you should plan on it taking anywhere from **two to six months** to see consistent visibility for your most important search terms.

facts.fact: The page's Google Business Profile to-do list advises uploading at least 10 high-quality photos (vendor's own recommendation).
facts.quote: Upload at least **10** high-quality photos.

facts.fact: The page says a business that works from home or serves customers at their location can hide its street address in the Google Business Profile and is then designated a Service Area Business (SAB).
facts.quote: you’ll have an option to hide your physical street address.

facts.fact: The page says the Service Area Business (SAB) designation is Google's specific label for businesses that work from home or travel to customers.
facts.quote: Google has a specific designation for this: a **Service Area Business (SAB)**.

facts.fact: The page states that a business does not have to pay for Google Ads to appear in the organic three-pack of Map Pack results.
facts.quote: you absolutely do not have to pay for Google Ads to earn a spot in the main, three-pack of organic Map Pack results.

facts.fact: The page says the NAP rule requires a business's name, address, and phone number to be exactly identical across all online listings.
facts.quote: Your business name, address, and phone number must be _exactly the same_ everywhere.

facts.fact: The page says a business may begin ranking for its own name in the Map Pack a few weeks after its Google Business Profile is verified (vendor's own estimate).
facts.quote: You'll often start ranking for your own business name in the Map Pack a few weeks after getting your Google Business Profile verified.

facts.fact: The page describes Adwave as an AI-powered platform for placing TV ads targeted to a small business's service area on streaming channels such as Hulu and ESPN (vendor's own claim).
facts.quote: reaching real customers on major streaming channels like Hulu and ESPN, right in the neighborhoods you work in every day.

facts.fact: Google sells ad space that appears in and around the Map Pack, such as sponsored map pins and Google Local Services Ads at the top of results, and these are a separate advertising product from organic Map Pack rankings.
facts.quote: However, Google _does_ sell ad space that appears in and around the Map Pack. You might see sponsored map pins or the Google Local Services Ads at the very top.
